draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: אַבְרָם is the subject of יָשַׁב. The verse contrasts where Abram settled, in the land of Canaan, with where Lot settled, in the cities of the plain.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68380:6, 68354:5, 68106:7, 66576:5.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “in.” The common-gender noun אֶרֶץ is singular and stands in construct before מוֹלַדְתּוֹ, “his birth.”

analysis.evidence: In אַבְרָם יָשַׁב בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן, “Abram lived in the land of Canaan,” כְּנָעַן follows the construct noun אֶרֶץ and names the territory where Abram lived.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun. The initial כ is part of the name. The word has no prefix or suffix.
